mnemonic: A waiter carries one cup of tea across an enormous lawn and sets it down on a single marked flagstone — not that table, this one. thîi pins a thing to its place: at, in, on. (↓ falling, the cup lands and settles)
headline: thîi…
scene: A white-gloved waiter bending to place a single porcelain teacup onto a small round table standing alone in the middle of a vast manicured lawn, a grand palace facade far behind. Long evening shadows stretching across the grass.

mnemonic: A German friend is asked about every plan for the week — the beach, the diving, the noodles — and answers each one with a short flat "Ja." Said the English way, jà. Every ja shoves the action into the future. That is จะ. (_ low and clipped, each ja a single short beat)
headline: Jà.
scene: A sunburnt traveller counting plans off on his fingers to a grinning backpacker sitting on a guesthouse step, who is nodding firmly with one thumb raised. Dive gear and a packed rucksack lean against the wall beside them. Bright morning light.

mnemonic: A polite man finishes his sentence, and a small golden crab pops onto the end of his words. The crab clicks its claws and says “ครับ!” making the sentence sound respectful and polite. Crab → ครับ → male polite particle used at the end of statements.

คะ and ค่ะ are the same soft syllable from the same woman; only the pitch differs. ค่ะ drops, and that is a full stop. คะ stays up high and holds the sentence open, because a question cannot end flat. The pitch is the question mark. (▲ high and taut, the sentence left hanging)
headline: …khá?
scene: A shopkeeper leans forward in her doorway and opens both arms wide, palms turned up, chin lifted and head tilted back in a questioning shrug. Baskets of fruit flank the step beside her. Warm afternoon light floods the open shopfront.

mnemonic: A SWAT team smashes through the door, rifles up — then the lead officer lowers his weapon, presses his palms together and says softly, "sa-WAT-dee." The whole squad copies him. Even a raid starts with hello. (— levels out flat and calm on dee)

A man in a gold suit walks round the room pointing at things and saying the same word each time: "Me. Me. Me." The car indoors, the chandelier, the dog — everything he points at, he has. mii is having, and there being. (— flat and level, the same note every time)
headline: Me. Me. Me.
scene: A man in a loud gold suit standing in a crowded living room jabbing his finger at a sports car parked absurdly indoors, then a chandelier, then a small dog. Every surface is piled with possessions. Bright glittering light.

mnemonic: A raccoon in hotel uniform bows to every guest and addresses each one the same way. Take the end of rac-coon and put breath behind the k: khun. It is the polite you that goes in front of anybody's name. (— flat and level, unfailingly polite)
headline: Khun…
scene: A raccoon standing upright in a braided doorman's uniform and white gloves, bowing deeply with one paw extended towards a startled guest with a suitcase. Brass luggage trolley, revolving door, polished marble lobby, warm chandelier light.

mnemonic: A man introduces himself and lays his open palm flat on his own chest, the voice climbing as it comes — phǒm. The palm on the chest is the word: a man saying I. (↑ rising, the voice lifts as the hand presses in)
headline: Phǒm.
scene: A Thai man in a pressed shirt at a formal introduction, standing straight and pressing his open palm flat against the centre of his own chest, head slightly bowed, smiling. Another man faces him with a hand half extended.

mnemonic: A giant ape sits on a mountain of treasure and pats each piece in turn: the crown, the anchor, the ship's bell. All of it is the treasure of Kong. khɔ̌ɔng hooks a thing to its owner. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he lifts each piece)
headline: …khɔ̌ɔng Kong.
scene: A colossal ape seated on a heaped mound of gold, crowns and ship's anchors on a rocky island, holding one glittering crown up to the light between two fingers, thoroughly satisfied. Tiny sailors stare up from a boat far below. Dawn sky.

mnemonic: Two friends on a bench are handed one cup between them and drink it together, heads almost touching, one on each side of it. Coffee with milk, her with him — everything paired goes through kàp. (_ low and flat, a cup set down on the table)
headline: …kàp…
scene: Two young friends on a low bench at a roadside drinks stall, leaning in from opposite sides to share a single tall iced coffee with two straws, shoulders touching, both laughing. Plastic stools, a steel kettle, dappled light through leaves.

skip_reason: No honest English anchor for lɛ́ — LA and lay both teach the wrong vowel, and the word is too short to carry a scene without one.

mnemonic: Rain hits at night and the whole street is suddenly indoors — faces at every lit window, nobody left outside. Say night and drop the t: nai. Everything is in. (— flat and level, the rain holding one note)
headline: nai
scene: A narrow Thai street in heavy night rain, empty of people, every shophouse window above glowing warm and crowded with faces looking out. Water sheets off the awnings and runs down the road, reflecting the lights.

mnemonic: A market vendor holds up a mango; the customer points at his own chest — "MY?" — voice climbing at the end the way an English question does. That climb is the question: ไหม turns any sentence into one. (↑ rising, the voice lifts like an eyebrow)

A man loads the car for the beach and stops short: a small nephew is already belted into the back seat with a towel round his neck. Dewey is coming too. dûai is the tag-along word — with, and also. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the boot slams)
headline: …dûai.
scene: A man in shorts leaning into the open rear door of a small car packed with beach gear, stopping short at the sight of a grinning boy already strapped into the back seat with a towel round his neck and a snorkel in one hand.

mnemonic: A khan sits on a high seat above the works and watches: the digging, the hauling, the raising of beams. He does not care who swings the pick, only that the doing goes on. kaan is the doing itself, wrapped round a verb. (— flat and level, the work goes on unchanged)
headline: kaan
scene: A fur-robed chieftain seated on a raised timber platform on a hillside, arms folded, watching an enormous construction site below where hundreds of labourers dig, carry baskets of earth and raise timber frames. Dust, coloured pennants, low golden light.

mnemonic: A vendor lifts a glass of orange tea and raises her eyebrows: this one? The customer nods once, hard. "Châi." Yes — chai, that is the one. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the nod)
headline: Châi.
scene: A customer drives his head down in one hard nod, his whole arm flung out to point at a tall glass of milky orange iced tea standing on the cart counter. Ice bucket, curling steam, sunlit street behind him.

mnemonic: A grandmother stands at the top of the lane and calls one long flat syllable down it — "Maaa" — and every child in the street turns and starts walking towards her. The word that brings things to you. (— flat and level, the call holds one note)
headline: Maaa—
scene: An elderly Thai woman standing at the end of a narrow village lane with one hand cupped at her mouth, calling. Four children in school uniform at the far end have turned mid-play and are running back towards her.

mnemonic: A landowner sweeps his arm over hills, rivers and villages running to the horizon: the whole estate. Take the tate off estate, put pra in front of it, and the estate has become a country. (↓ the second half falls hard, the arm sweeping down)
headline: pra-tʰêet
scene: A man in a wide hat standing on a high terrace with one arm sweeping across an enormous landscape of rice terraces, a winding river, distant temple spires and blue mountains fading to the horizon. Early morning haze, warm light.

skip_reason: No English word carries /kwaa/ — quarter, qualm and kwai each shift the vowel or add a consonant.

mnemonic: The cow lows exactly when the pail is set down, not a moment before. Say moo with the lips pulled wide in a grin instead of pushed forward and you have mɯ̂a: the word that marks the moment something happens. (↓ falling, the moo drops away at the end)
headline: mɯ̂a…
scene: A farmer swings a steel pail down onto the straw beneath a cow, arm extended, body low over a milking stool. The cow's head is thrown back, mouth wide. Cold blue dawn through the open shed door, a lamp hanging above.

skip_reason: ná's only English sound-alike is "nah", which teaches refusal — the opposite of a softening particle.

mnemonic: A road crew counts its men by the traffic cones on their heads: one cone, one man. Lose a cone and you have lost a person. khon is a person, and the word you count people with. (— flat and level, counting in an even voice)
headline: One cone, one khon.
scene: A row of road workers in orange vests standing to attention on a closed carriageway, each with a traffic cone upside down on his head like a hat, while a foreman walks the line pointing at each in turn.

mnemonic: A phone call in the middle of a market: where are you? The answer is one flat low word — yùu — and an arm goes straight up above the crowd so the caller can see where he is. yùu is being somewhere. (_ low and flat, the voice sits still like the man)
headline: …yùu.
scene: A man stands dead still in a packed night market with one arm stretched straight up above the heads around him and a phone pressed to his other ear. The crowd streams past him in a blur. String lights, food steam, warm night.

skip_reason: The ɯa vowel has no English carrier here — rung and wrong both teach a different vowel, and there is no word that fits.

mnemonic: A baker slaps a dark loaf on the counter and the customer stares at it: a rye? What is it? à-rai is the question you ask when you cannot name the thing in front of you. (— the second syllable levels out flat, eyebrows still up)
headline: à-rai?
scene: A bakery counter where the baker has just set down a dense dark loaf. The customer leans over it with head tilted and brow furrowed, one finger hovering above the crust without touching it.

mnemonic: Two hikers on a ridge; one points down at a hut in the valley where tea and a piece of nan bread are waiting. thîi is the place and nân is that one — thîi-nân, that place over there. (↓↓ both syllables drop, like the pointing arm)
headline: thîi-nân.
scene: Two hikers on a high rocky ridge at dusk, one with an arm fully outstretched pointing down into the valley at a tiny lit hut with smoke rising from it. Packs on their backs, wind in their jackets, layered mountains behind.

mnemonic: A man stops dead at the end of the high board, gripped by a qualm — nothing you can hold, but suddenly the whole matter is the size of the pool. khwaam turns a feeling into a thing: the -ness stuck on the front of a word. (— flat and level, the word gives nothing away)
headline: khwaam…
scene: A man standing frozen at the end of a high diving board, toes over the edge, arms half raised, staring down at the blue rectangle of water far below. Empty tiered seating all round, harsh poolside light, small ripples on the surface.

mnemonic: A man bites into a chewy sweet and his jaw locks shut. He waves both arms at the stall keeper, eyes wide, unable to get the word out — chûai, help me. (↓ falling, the cry drops away as his mouth clamps)
headline: Chûai!
scene: A man at a sweets stall with his jaw clamped shut on an enormous toffee, cheeks bulging, both arms waving frantically above his head, eyes wide with alarm. The stall keeper leans over trays of sticky sweets, laughing. Bright market awning, midday.

mnemonic: The waiter whips the plate away the moment the last mouthful is gone — done, finished, lɛ́ɛo. Say the vowel in cat and slide it into ow. Everything that has already happened ends with it. (▲ high and taut, the plate snatched away)
headline: …lɛ́ɛo!
scene: A restaurant table where a waiter's hand is whipping an empty plate away just as the diner sets down his fork, the diner's other hand still half raised in surprise. Crumpled napkin, empty glass, warm evening light through a window.

mnemonic: ไหน and ไหม are twins with the same rising climb — only the first sound differs. ไหม (M) asks "is it so?"; ไหน (N) asks "where?". Picture two identical signposts at a fork: the M arm points at a question mark, the N arm points at a map. Same rise in the voice, different letter, different question. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the eyes search)

At the end of the row the farmer tips the plough up and puts the question to the field: another furrow, or nothing? plàao means blank, empty — so rɯ̌ɯ-plàao is literally "or empty?", the yes-or-no bolted to the end of a sentence. (_ the second word drops low, the plough set down)
headline: …rɯ̌ɯ-plàao?
scene: A farmer at the end of a half-ploughed paddy at sunset, one hand resting on the upturned handle of a wooden plough, looking back along the furrow. Half the field is turned dark earth, half is bare dry ground.

mnemonic: She pushes the jars of pickled mango to the very back of the high shelf where nobody will get at them. Why keep so many? Because wái is exactly that — putting a thing aside to keep. (▲ high and taut, said over her shoulder)
headline: …wái.
scene: A woman on a step stool pushing a row of sealed glass jars of yellow pickled fruit to the very back of a high kitchen shelf, glancing back over her shoulder. The shelf is already crowded with jars.

mnemonic: Someone asks how he does it and the man taps his own chest with the butt of his cue: because he is a pro. That is the whole answer — prɔ́, the word that hands you the reason. (▲ high and taut, snapped out with the tap of the cue)
headline: …prɔ́.
scene: A man in a waistcoat thumps the butt of his snooker cue against his own chest, chin lifted, shoulders thrown back, one eyebrow raised. Behind him a green baize table sits under a low hanging lamp, smoke drifting through the beam.

mnemonic: A kangaroo in a quiz booth thumps the buzzer before the question is finished. The roo knows. rúu is knowing a fact, and this one knows the lot. (▲ high and taut, the buzzer's flat bright note)
headline: Rúu!
scene: A kangaroo sitting upright in a brightly lit television quiz booth, one paw slamming a big red buzzer, the other tucked smugly across its chest. Two human contestants in the neighbouring booths stare at it, mouths open. Studio lights, glossy desk.

mnemonic: An old gray-haired man in flashy party clothes insists, “I’m still young! The night is still young!” A confused young person looks at him, clearly seeing he’s not young anymore. Young → ยัง (— neutral, ongoing) → still / not yet finished.

The foreman raises one thumb and the whole line starts moving — saws, hammers, sparks. Say thumb with a hard t and no lisp: tham, to make, to do. Thumb up and it gets made. (— flat and level, the same steady note as the machines)
headline: tham!
scene: A workshop foreman on a gantry above a busy production floor, one thumb raised high, mouth open in a shout. Below him men bend over benches, sparks flying from a grinder, timber moving along rollers. Shafts of dusty light from high windows.

mnemonic: The rain starts and the cow decides, against all precedent, to let herself into the kitchen. A whole cow through the doorway — khâo, to enter, to go in. (↓ falling, the voice drops as she ducks under the lintel)
headline: Khâo.
scene: A large brown cow halfway through the open back door of a village kitchen, head and shoulders inside, ducking under the low lintel, while a woman at the stove turns round with a wooden spoon raised.

skip_reason: The ɤː vowel has no English equivalent; loi, looey and learn all teach a different vowel.

mnemonic: The family has moved into the barn and made it home: a bed in one stall, a kettle on a crate, washing strung between the beams. Say barn without the r — bâan — the house you live in. (↓ falling, the voice drops like a door closing for the night)
headline: bâan.
scene: The inside of a big timber barn made into a family home: a bed made up in one stall, a kettle steaming on a crate, laundry strung between the roof beams, a child playing on a rug on the straw floor.

mnemonic: He cannot get the sentence out, so he puts the words down one at a time like stones across a stream until they reach the far bank. Say put with a long oo: phûut, to speak. (↓ falling, each word dropped into place)
headline: phûut.
scene: A man crouches at the edge of a shallow stream and lowers a flat stepping stone into the water with both hands. A line of stones already reaches halfway to the far bank. Morning mist over the reeds, soft grey light on the water.

mnemonic: An old janitor lifts a keyring so heavy it needs both hands — hundreds of keys fanning out like a metal peacock. Someone asks the only sensible question: "Kìi?" How many keys? (_ low and flat, a short blunt question)
A boy slides down a very long slide from the top of a hill. As he rushes downward he shouts, “This is a LONG way down!” Long → ลง → down / put down / get off. (— neutral drop)

The tailor runs the tape round the customer and calls the number out: one body, measured. tuua is the body itself, and the word you count animals and bodies with — two arms, two legs, one tuua. (— flat and level, the tape held straight)
headline: …tuua.
scene: A tailor kneeling to run a cloth tape measure round the waist of a customer standing on a low wooden box with both arms held straight out, pins gripped in the tailor's lips.

mnemonic: A boy at the zoo railing points at the yak and will not be moved: he wants it, wants to take it home. jàak is wanting — a long low ache of a word with a yak at the end of it. (_ low and flat, the want settles in and stays)
headline: jàak…
scene: A small boy gripping a zoo railing with both hands, cheek pressed between the bars, staring longingly at a huge shaggy yak chewing in its enclosure. His mother tugs gently at his hood from behind. Grey overcast light, damp ground.

mnemonic: A small boy grabs an enormous weathered hand — a bear's paw of a hand — and says "Phôo." The hand belongs to his father, and it swallows his whole fist. (↓ falling, warm and settled)

A fortune teller peers over her cards, jabs a finger across the table and says "Ah — YOU!" She has guessed your age to the year, and the YOU comes out bright and hard and stays up there. aa-yú is the number of years you have. (▲ the second syllable snaps up high on YOU and holds)
headline: Ah — YOU!
scene: An old fortune teller lunges across a spread of cards and throws one arm straight out at the viewer, finger extended, rings on every finger, eyes wide and certain. Heavy red cloth drapes the booth behind her. Candlelight, deep shadow.

mnemonic: Hum an ng in the nose, then say earn: ngɤɤn. Old money was silver, so the same word does both jobs — the dull silver coins counted out of a pay packet at the end of the week are what you earned. (— flat and level, one coin, one note)
headline: ngɤɤn.
scene: A pair of hands counting old silver coins out of a small cloth pay packet onto a worn wooden table, a short stack already built beside them. A rolled shirt cuff, dim window light behind, dust in the air.

mnemonic: Hum an ng in the nose, then say earn — ngɤɤn, the money you earn. Notes counted onto the tray one at a time; the same word whether it is coins, notes or a salary. (— flat and level, an even count)
headline: ngɤɤn.
scene: A market trader's hands counting gold coins one by one from a fat roll onto a metal tray on the counter, a queue of customers waiting beyond. Overhead strip light, produce crates stacked behind, late afternoon.

mnemonic: A mouse crosses the kitchen floor and the cook shrieks — eek — then another, then another. Each one gets its own eek. ʔìik is more: again, another one. (_ low and flat, and by the third mouse the eek has gone tired)
headline: …ʔìik.
scene: A cook standing on a kitchen chair with her apron gathered in both fists, looking down at three mice crossing the tiled floor in single file, her expression more weary than frightened. Copper pans, a pot left steaming on the stove.

skip_reason: No English word carries tʰaa- plus ŋ — thong and tang each shift the vowel, and thong also swaps the consonant.

mnemonic: A father hoists a toddler onto his shoulders and answers the neighbour's question with one word: his lûuk. Say Luke and let the voice fall — your child, and the young of anything. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the boy is swung up)
headline: …lûuk.
scene: A father in a village lane swinging a laughing toddler up onto his shoulders, both hands round the child's ankles, while a neighbour leans over a low fence smiling. Chickens scattering, washing on a line, late golden light.

mnemonic: He carries her rucksack as well as his own up every step of the hill and will not hand either back. The first sound of rucksack is rák: love, done rather than said. (▲ high and taut, said through the effort)
headline: rák.
scene: A young man toiling up a long flight of temple steps with two large rucksacks, one on his back and one across his front, sweat on his face, while a young woman climbs easily beside him with empty hands, laughing.

mnemonic: Two brothers stand back to back to settle who is taller. The taller one is P — top of the list — "Phîi" — and his hand comes down flat on his brother's head to prove it. (↓ falling, the hand settles the matter)

The diver hesitates on the rock and her friend flicks a hand at the water: go on, see, just jump. sì is that flick — the little push on the end of an order that turns it into encouragement. (_ low and clipped, over before it starts)
headline: …sì!
scene: Two teenagers on a river rock in swimwear; one stands at the edge with arms wrapped round herself, the other sits behind flicking an open hand towards the green water below, grinning. Jungle bank, sun flashing on the water.

mnemonic: Someone tells you something you flatly do not believe and all you can manage is a rising grunt — rə̌ə? It is the vowel of English er with an r on the front and the voice climbing. The eyebrows do the rest. (↑ rising, voice and eyebrows climb together)
headline: Rə̌ə?
scene: Two women at a café table; one leans back with both eyebrows shot up and her chin tucked in, staring at the other, who is still talking with her hands mid-gesture. Half-drunk iced coffees, condensation rings on the table, bright window light.

mnemonic: An orc is thrown out of the tavern and lands in the street — out, and staying out. ɔ̀ɔk is going out: the exit, the way out, the thing that leaves. (_ low and flat, the sound of the door shutting behind him)
headline: ʔɔ̀ɔk!
scene: A heavy tavern door swinging shut while a large green-skinned brute in patched leather sits stunned in the muddy street outside, his helmet rolling away. A pair of hands still visible at the doorframe. Lantern light spilling out, wet cobbles, night.

mnemonic: A proper row over the garden fence: one family on this side, one on that, and every second word is us — us, we, our lot. rao is we, and it sounds like the row itself. (— flat and level, both sides holding the same note)
headline: rao.
scene: Two families leaning over a low garden fence at each other, arms thrown wide, mouths open mid-shout, each group pressed shoulder to shoulder on its own side. Washing lines, scattered toys, hot bright afternoon.

mnemonic: A friend suddenly grabs your shoulder and shouts, “Duuuuude, look!” He points excitedly at something happening in front of you, forcing your attention toward it. “Duuuuude” → ดู → to look, watch, or observe. (— neutral)

One engine still running on an empty airfield long after everything else has shut down, alone out there in the dark. ʔeeng tacks itself onto a person and means by themselves: he did it eeng, he alone. (— flat and level, the engine holding one note)
headline: …ʔeeng.
scene: A single small propeller aircraft on a vast empty airfield at dusk with its propeller spinning and navigation lights on, every other aircraft in the row dark and chocked. Long shadows, orange horizon, nobody in sight.

skip_reason: The ɯa vowel has no English equivalent; dune and dwan both teach a different vowel.

mnemonic: It is noon and nothing is happening. He lies flat and the afternoon goes on and on — "nooon" — never rising, never falling. (— completely level; the voice lies down too)

A chef scans a row of identical mangoes, then slaps one down on the board — "nîi lɛ̀!" — that one. The word is over before it starts, cut off short like the slap itself. (_ low and clipped, stopped dead at the end)
The same see as สิ, but snapped out high and quick between friends — and the hand on your back is harder. สิ nudges; ซิ shoves. Go on, do it. (▲ high and taut, a short bright shove)
headline: …sí!
scene: A boy on the edge of a wooden jetty with both arms out for balance, another boy behind him with both palms planted flat between his shoulder blades, laughing and pushing. River water below, a moored longtail boat beyond, hot midday light.

mnemonic: A boy carries an old woman's shopping across the road and walks off before she can thank him — a good deed. Take the d off the end and you have dii: good. (— flat and level, said without fuss)
headline: dii.
scene: A teenage boy setting two heavy shopping bags down on a kerb beside an elderly woman and already turning away with a hand half raised, while she reaches after him. Busy street behind, traffic, warm late light.

mnemonic: A player pulls the one block holding the whole tower up; therefore — and it is a proper therefore — it comes down across the table. Take the first sound of Jenga and say it with the lips spread flat: tɕɯng. (— flat and level, said into the silence after the crash)
headline: tɕɯng.
scene: A wooden block tower collapsing across a table, blocks tumbling and bouncing, a young woman's hand frozen in the air still holding the single block she pulled, her face caught between horror and laughter. Friends leaning back, drinks, warm lamplight.

mnemonic: A rope tore in two and the sailor splices the ends back together, turn by turn, one length carried on into the next. tɔ̀ɔ is joining on: continue, connect, and so much each. (_ low and flat, the steady pull of the splice)
headline: tɔ̀ɔ…
scene: Close view of a sailor's weathered hands splicing two frayed rope ends together on a boat deck, the strands interwoven halfway, a marlinspike gripped in his teeth. Coiled rope, wet planks, bright sea glare behind.

mnemonic: A shopkeeper slaps a fat red starburst over the old one in the window and a LOT has come off. lót is the cut itself — prices, speed, weight, volume, anything that comes down — but the voice does not come down with it. It snaps up bright and stays up. (▲ high and taut, called over his shoulder from the step stool)
headline: lót!
scene: A grinning shopkeeper on a step stool inside a shopfront window, pressing a huge red starburst sticker over a smaller one on the glass, the corner of the old one still peeling up. Shoppers outside press in to look.

mnemonic: You jàai for your chai. The two words sit almost on top of each other — the drink and the paying for it — so every cup you buy is a free rehearsal. (_ low, the flat sound of coins going down on the counter)

The same cow as เข้า, at a different pitch: this one climbs. Asked who left the gate open, the farmer just lifts his chin at the man leaning on it — khǎo, him. (↑ rising, the chin and the voice go up together)
headline: Khǎo.
scene: A farmer standing in a yard with arms folded, lifting his chin towards a sheepish young man leaning on an open gate, while a cow wanders out through it behind him. Muddy yard, wooden fence, flat morning light.

mnemonic: The grand pooh-bah arrives: sash, medals, and a chair carried by four straining men. phûu is the one-who — put it in front of a trade and you have the person who does it. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the weight of the title)
headline: phûu…
scene: A pompous official in a sash heavy with medals being carried through a crowd on an ornate chair by four straining bearers, chin high, one hand raised in a small wave. Coloured pennants, dust, bright ceremonial daylight.

mnemonic: The twin of หน่อย, but the voice stays up high. A boy holds the bag upside down over his palm: one chilli left, nɔ́ɔi, that is all there is. (▲ high and taut, held up like the chilli itself)
headline: nɔ́ɔi.
scene: A boy raises a nearly empty paper bag high overhead and shakes it upside down over his open palm, where one small red chilli has landed. Kitchen shelves and a steaming pot stand behind him. Warm afternoon light through a window.

mnemonic: The night watchman stops dead on the stair — hark, if that was a footstep, someone is in the house. hàak is the if that opens the sentence: everything hangs on what he hears next. (_ low and flat, said under the breath)
headline: hàak…
scene: A night watchman frozen halfway up a dark wooden staircase, lantern lowered, head turned to listen, one foot still raised above the next step. Long shadows up the wall, a half-open door above him, faint moonlight.

mnemonic: An old man keeps a jar on the sill and drops one dried pea into it every birthday. The jar is nearly full. pii is a year — count the peas and you have his age. (— flat and level, one pea, one note)
headline: …pii.
scene: An old man's hands dropping a single dried pea into a tall glass jar almost full of them on a windowsill, beside a slice of cake with one candle burning. Warm low sunlight through the window, a faded curtain.

mnemonic: A boy wheels a bicycle out of the shop and will not let anyone else touch the handlebars: mine, and never anyone's before. mài is new, and it sounds exactly like that my. (_ low and flat, said with both hands on the bars)
headline: …mài.
scene: A boy gripping the handlebars of a gleaming new bicycle just outside a shop doorway, shoulders hunched protectively, while two other children reach towards it. A shop window full of bicycles behind, hard sunlight on the pavement.

mnemonic: The cake is cut into slices and a sugar swan is set on each one — one swan, one portion, and nobody gets two. sùan is the share: the section, the part of the whole. (_ low and flat, the knife going straight down)
headline: …sùan.
scene: An overhead view of a large round cake cut into eight even slices on a table, a small white sugar swan standing on each slice, hands reaching in from several sides. A bright party cloth, scattered crumbs.

mnemonic: The parcel comes out of the back of the van and he catches it against his chest without breaking stride. ráp is receiving — taking what comes at you — and it lands with a flat rap. (▲ high and taut, the smack of the catch)
headline: Ráp!
scene: A delivery man on the pavement catching a wrapped parcel against his chest with knees bent, as another man hurls it from the open back of a van. Motion blur on the parcel, stacked boxes in the van, grey morning street.

mnemonic: A line of orange-robed monks at dawn, bowls out, and the first sound of prayer already in the air. phrá is the monk himself — and the word you put in front of anything holy. (▲ high and taut, one bright syllable)
headline: phrá.
scene: A line of monks in orange robes walking barefoot down a misty street at dawn with alms bowls held at their chests, while a kneeling woman places rice into the first bowl. Soft grey light, shuttered shopfronts, bare feet on wet ground.

mnemonic: A hall of empty chairs and abandoned music stands, and only the piano still playing — only that, nothing else. Take the pian from piano and hum the end in your nose: phiiang, only. (— flat and level, one instrument holding one note)
headline: phiiang…
scene: A vast concert hall with rows of empty chairs and abandoned music stands in darkness, one grand piano lit by a single overhead lamp with a pianist still playing. Dust drifting in the beam of light.

mnemonic: The shopkeeper asks what size and the customer holds up a gnat between finger and thumb: that big. kha-nàat is size — from a gnat to an elephant, it is the same word. (_ the second syllable drops low and flat, the fingers pinching shut)
headline: kha-nàat.
scene: A woman raises one hand in front of a plain pale wall and pinches her thumb and forefinger almost shut, squinting hard at the tiny gap between them, her whole face leaning in toward her fingers. Soft even light, nothing else in the frame.

mnemonic: A boy picks up a violin he has never touched and plays it perfectly first time. The old teacher points at him and names him on the spot: nák — the one with the knack, the person of that trade. (▲ high and taut, one bright word)
headline: nák…
scene: An elderly music teacher in a cluttered practice room pointing at a small boy who is holding a violin under his chin mid-bow, eyes closed. The other pupils have stopped playing and turned to stare.

mnemonic: The whole crew is out bringing in the crop — grandmother, parents, children, all bent over the same rows. A family is a crop-crew: khrɔ̂ɔp-khruua. (↓ the first half drops hard, the load coming down)
headline: khrɔ̂ɔp-khruua.
scene: Three generations of one family harvesting a rice paddy together at dusk: an old woman bent over the stalks, two adults carrying bundled sheaves on a shoulder pole, two children dragging a basket. Flooded field reflecting an orange sky.

mnemonic: Ask the hundred-year-old woman how she managed it and she taps her temple: cheer, and wit. chii-wít is a life — the whole span of one, in two syllables. (▲ the second syllable snaps up high as her finger taps)
headline: chii-wít.
scene: A very old woman on a wooden porch chair, laughing, tapping her own temple with one crooked finger while three young people crouch around her listening. Cats on the steps, potted plants, soft late afternoon light.

mnemonic: A basketball player stands back to back with a small boy and the measuring hand has to climb and climb. Say soon and hum the end into your nose: sǔung, tall. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the hand)
headline: sǔung.
scene: A very tall basketball player standing back to back with a small boy in a school gym while a teacher on a step stool reaches up with a flat hand to mark the top of the player's head.

mnemonic: The bus swings round the bend and every standing passenger leans the same way; at the next stop they all get off and change to another bus. Put a p on lean — plìan — and you have changing, switching, transferring. (_ low and flat, the lean held steady through the bend)
headline: plìan.
scene: The interior of a crowded bus taking a sharp bend, every standing passenger leaning the same way in unison with hands on the overhead rail. Through the windows another bus waits at a stop ahead. Hot daylight, dust on the glass.

mnemonic: ต่อ joins on and ไป goes: together they mean carry on to the one after this. The relay runner takes the baton and is gone before the first has stopped — tɔ̀ɔ-pai, next. (_ the first syllable drops low, the second runs off with him)
headline: tɔ̀ɔ-pai.
scene: A relay handover on a running track: one runner at full stretch pressing a baton into the open backward-reaching hand of the next, who is already accelerating away. Painted lanes, a blurred stadium behind, harsh floodlight.

mnemonic: A hen picks one spot in the whole yard and settles into it; no other spot will do. Say hen and let the end hum in your nose — hɛ̀ng — the place, that particular spot. (_ low and flat, the hen settling into the dust)
headline: hɛ̀ng.
scene: A single brown hen settled in a shallow dust hollow in the exact middle of an otherwise empty farmyard, feathers fluffed and eyes half shut, while other hens wander round the edges. Hard midday sun, a sharp shadow beneath her.

mnemonic: The lid comes off the basket and the fish inside is longer than the man holding it — yikes. Cut it down to yài and you have big: the fish, the house, the boss. (_ low and flat, the word lands like the fish on the deck)
headline: yài!
scene: A fisherman on a dock struggling to hold up an enormous fish longer than he is tall, knees buckling, mouth open in astonishment, while a small crowd of onlookers backs away. Bright harbour light, boats and nets behind.

mnemonic: The same phǒm a man uses for himself is the word for the hair on his head: one palm goes to the chest, the other to the crown. The barber lifts the mirror and there it is, what is left of his phǒm. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the hand)
headline: phǒm.
scene: A barber holding a round hand mirror behind a seated man's head so he can see the back of his fresh haircut, the man patting the top of his own head with one hand.

mnemonic: The grandmother turns the sock over to darn the other side — this side done, that side still holed. dâan is a side, a face, an aspect: whichever one is turned towards you. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the sock is flipped)
headline: dâan.
scene: An old woman by a window turning a woollen sock over a wooden darning mushroom, needle raised in one hand, a basket of mending at her feet. Soft grey daylight, a worn armchair, spectacles low on her nose.

mnemonic: One dew drop on the whole leaf, the only one left on the whole bush, and it holds the entire garden upside down inside it. Say dee, then ow, and run them together: diiaw — one, single, the only one there is. (— flat and level, nothing moves at all)
headline: diiaw.
scene: Extreme close view of a single large dew drop hanging from the tip of one green leaf at dawn, the blurred garden behind reflected upside down inside it. The rest of the leaf is dry. Cool blue morning light.

mnemonic: Say moo with the lips pulled wide in a grin, then hum the end: mɯang. The town is wherever the cattle market is — one flat bellow carries over the rooftops and everyone knows which town they are in. (— flat and level, one long note held over the roofs)
headline: mɯang.
scene: A hillside view down over a Thai market town at dusk: tiled rooftops, a temple spire, and a cattle pen at the edge where buffalo stand packed together, one with its head raised. Smoke from cooking fires, warm haze.

mnemonic: Every head in the barber's chairs has a different cut and every cut has its own song — the quiff hums, the bob swings, the crop marches. Ask for a song and you get a style. soŋ is the shape a thing is styled into. (— flat and level, everyone on the same note)
headline: soŋ.
scene: A barber shop where four customers in a row of chairs all have wildly different hairstyles and are all singing with mouths open, while the barber conducts them with his comb. Mirrors, chrome chairs, bright strip lighting.

mnemonic: The tattooist stops the needle dead and cuts the line off clean rather than carry it round the arm. tàt is cutting — hair, cloth, price, a line stopped short. (_ low and flat, the word cut off as sharply as the line)
headline: tàt.
scene: Close view of a tattooist's gloved hands lifting the needle away from a forearm, a bold black line ending abruptly mid-curve on the skin. Ink pots, a wiped paper towel, harsh angled lamp light.

mnemonic: He takes the turning everyone warned him about and walks straight into the pit, mud up to his chest, looking up at the path he should have taken. phìt is wrong — the wrong one, the mistake. (_ low and flat, the bottom of the pit)
headline: phìt.
scene: A man standing chest-deep in a muddy pit in a jungle path, arms out for balance, looking up at the proper trail curving safely past above him. Broken branches around the pit edge, green shade, damp earth.

mnemonic: The gatekeeper stands with folded arms and will not open up until John comes — not a minute earlier. tɕon is the until: everything holds still right up to that point. (— flat and level, the wait unchanging)
headline: …tɕon…
scene: A uniformed gatekeeper standing motionless with folded arms inside a locked factory gate at night, the headlights of an approaching car just beginning to light his face. Empty yard behind, rain on the tarmac, one sodium lamp.

mnemonic: The tow truck hooks up one car and no more: that much, and that is all of it. tʰâw is as-much-as and nán is that — put them together and you have only. (▲ the last syllable snaps up high, the hook locking on)
headline: …tʰâw nán.
scene: A tow truck on a night street with a single small car hoisted on its hook while a whole row of other parked cars sits untouched behind it. The driver leans out of the cab holding up one finger.

mnemonic: A bucket chain at a house fire: the pan of water goes from hand to hand, past each person and on to the next. Say pan with the long ah of father — phàan — to pass by, to go through. (_ low and flat, the steady rhythm of the chain)
headline: phàan.
scene: A line of villagers strung between a well and a burning wooden house at night, passing a metal pan of water hand to hand, faces lit orange. Smoke and sparks rising, buckets scattered on the ground.

mnemonic: The photograph is torn in two and each half holds a different part of the day: the morning in one hand, the evening in the other. tɔɔn is the stretch of time you mean — the bit you tore out. (— flat and level, both halves held up the same)
headline: tɔɔn…
scene: Two hands holding up the torn halves of one photograph side by side, one half showing a sunlit breakfast table and the other the same table by lamplight. Plain dark background, the torn edge ragged between them.

mnemonic: Something under the floorboards reeks and the whole family stands in the doorway calling for the landlord, over and over. rîiak is to call — to call out, to call someone, to call a thing by its name. (↓ falling, each shout drops away at the end)
headline: Rîiak!
scene: A family clustered in an open doorway holding their noses with one hand and waving with the other, shouting up the street, lifted floorboards behind them in a dim hallway. Evening light, a cat fleeing past their feet.

mnemonic: One photograph of papa on the wall, and it is the only picture anybody has of him. Say papa and stop halfway — phâap — a picture, an image, the thing that keeps a face. (↓ falling, the voice drops the way a hand lowers a frame)
headline: phâap.
scene: A single framed portrait of an old man hanging alone on a bare wooden wall, with a small shelf beneath it holding incense and a marigold garland. Dust turning in a shaft of light from a high window.

mnemonic: An aunt reads to the whole room without once looking up, one finger moving down the page, and nobody dares interrupt. Say aunt and drop the t: àan, to read. (_ low and flat, a quiet voice that never lifts)
headline: àan.
scene: An elderly aunt in an armchair reading aloud from an open book on her lap, one finger tracing down the page, four children sitting cross-legged on the floor around her, rapt. Lamplight, drawn curtains, evening.

mnemonic: The teacher claps once and every child turns round and comes straight back from the far end of the field. klàp is going back — back home, back the way you came. (_ low and flat, one clap, no echo)
headline: klàp!
scene: A teacher at the edge of a school field with hands just brought together in a clap, while thirty children scattered across the grass all turn at once and begin running back towards her. Dust, long shadows, late afternoon.

mnemonic: A globe spins on a low table and the boy stops it dead with one finger. Say low and put a k on the end — lôok — the world, the whole of it under one fingertip. (↓ falling, the spin slowing and stopping)
headline: lôok.
scene: A boy leaning over a large old spinning globe on a low table in a dim study, stopping it with one extended finger, his face lit by a desk lamp. Crowded shelves and a brass telescope in the shadows behind him.

mnemonic: ráp is the catch; dâi in front of it says it actually landed. The parcel smacks into his palm and stays there — dâi-ráp, received, got. (▲ the second word snaps up high with the smack)
headline: dâi-ráp.
scene: A man on a doorstep with a parcel just landing hard in his open palm, his fingers closing round it, a courier already turning away down the path. Motion blur on the courier, a wet garden path, grey morning.

mnemonic: Two lines of men lean back on the same rope, one line each side of the mud, and fie on the other lot. Each fàai is a side — and there are only ever two worth naming. (_ low and flat, the strain held steady)
headline: fàai.
scene: A tug of war across a muddy ditch at a village fair: two lines of men leaning far back on one rope, heels dug in, faces straining, a crowd shouting on both banks. Churned mud, bright overcast light.

mnemonic: Two people come round the same corner at the same instant and pop — face to face, nose to nose, both stopped dead. phóp is meeting, and it is over in one syllable. (▲ high and taut, gone in an instant)
headline: Phóp!
scene: Two people colliding face to face at a blind corner of a narrow alley, both rocking back on their heels with arms flung up, dropped shopping bursting on the ground between them. Washing overhead, hard midday light.

mnemonic: เข้า is to enter and ใจ is the heart. An idea you understand is one that got through the door and sat down inside you. khâo-tɕai — in it went. (↓ the first syllable drops hard, the door swinging shut behind it)
headline: khâo-tɕai.
scene: A cutaway of a small wooden house with a warm glowing interior, a figure stepping over the threshold out of the dark into the light and shaking rain from a coat.

mnemonic: She seals her song inside the envelope and pushes it through the slot of the competition box. sòng is sending: a letter, a parcel, a child off to school. (_ low and flat, the envelope dropping out of sight)
headline: sòng.
scene: A woman's hand pushing a sealed envelope through the slot of a large wooden competition box in a hotel lobby, a queue behind her holding envelopes of their own. Polished floor, potted palms, bright lobby light.

mnemonic: She carries the whole tower of baskets up the steps on one upturned hand and never touches the rail. Say too with the lips pulled wide in a grin — thɯ̌ɯ — to hold, to carry, to keep hold of. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the load)
headline: thɯ̌ɯ.
scene: A woman climbing temple steps balancing a stack of six woven baskets on one upturned palm above her shoulder, the other arm out for balance, chin level. A stone naga balustrade, green trees, bright morning light.

skip_reason: No English word carries khuuan; quan- and kwan- sound-alikes all shift the vowel.

mnemonic: The pan handle comes away in his hand and the whole dinner goes across the floor — pan-hǎa. The ha on the end climbs like a question nobody can answer. (↑ the second syllable climbs, both hands thrown up)
headline: pan-hǎa!
scene: A cook in a home kitchen holding a detached pan handle in one hand and staring down at an upturned pan and a curry spreading across the tiles, a cat already approaching the edge of the mess. Hard overhead light.

skip_reason: The only English sound-alike, "nah", teaches refusal — the opposite of "worth doing".

mnemonic: The moon in the sky and the moon in the paddy water — the same thing twice over. Say moon with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward: mɯ̌an, like, the same as. (↑ rising, the voice climbs from the water to the sky)
headline: mɯ̌an.
scene: A flooded rice paddy at night, perfectly still, with the full moon overhead and its identical reflection in the water, a lone farmer silhouetted between them on a narrow bund. Deep blue night, faint mist.

mnemonic: A gigantic cinnamon bun is sitting on top of a skyscraper. People point upward and shout, “Look! The bun is ON the building!” Bun → บน → on / on top of. (— neutral)

The trader drops the coin on the stone and listens: real gold rings — jing. The fake one beside it only thuds. tɕing is true, real, genuine, and it is the sound the real one makes. (— flat and level, one clear note)
headline: tɕing!
scene: A market trader dropping a gold coin onto a stone slab at his stall, head tilted to listen with one eye closed, a second coin lying flat and dull beside it. Brass scales, cloth pouches, close crop, warm low light.

mnemonic: Everyone squeezes into the one room for the photograph, and the last two run in and drop to the floor at the front. rûam is joining in, taking part, all of it together. (↓ falling, the voice drops as they settle)
headline: rûam.
scene: Twenty people crammed into a small living room for a group photograph, the front row kneeling, two latecomers sliding in at the edges, everyone laughing. A cat on the back of the sofa. Warm lamplight, flash catching faces.

mnemonic: The butcher lifts a long chain of sausages across the stall and names them down the line, one example after another. tɕʰên is for-example: this one, and this one, and this. (↓ falling, the voice drops at each link)
headline: tɕʰên…
scene: A butcher holding up a long linked chain of sausages at arm's length across his stall, pointing at each link in turn with his other hand while a customer follows his finger. Hooks, a marble counter, cold bright market light.

mnemonic: À la carte: no set menu, nothing bundled, every single dish standing on its own board at its own price. The waiter holds up three fingers for three dishes and charges for each. lá is exactly that — so much each, one price per item. (▲ high and taut, snapped out straight after the number)
headline: …lá.
scene: A waiter setting down three separate small dishes on a restaurant table, each on its own little wooden board and spaced well apart, while the diner holds up three fingers. White cloth, brass cutlery, warm evening light.

mnemonic: A cat on a windowsill lifts its nose, reads the air and knows the rain is coming an hour before you do. aa-kàat is both the air and what it is doing — weather. (_ the second syllable settles low, like the cat)
Everything she has ever kept is in that cupboard: string, buttons, the good tin. Say kept and drop the t — kèp — to put away and keep. (_ low and flat, the door pushed quietly shut)
headline: kèp.
scene: An old woman easing a crowded cupboard door shut with both hands, the shelves inside packed with tins, jars, folded cloth and coiled string. A dim kitchen, one window, soft grey daylight.

mnemonic: A string of firecrackers and only some of them go off — bang, bang, a gap, then one more. bâang is some: a few of them, not the lot. (↓ falling, each bang drops away into the gap)
headline: bâang.
scene: A string of red firecrackers hanging from a doorway, three of them blown apart mid-burst with smoke and scraps flying, the rest still whole on the string. Children with hands over their ears behind. Bright daylight.

mnemonic: The old man will not be helped up the step; his daughter hovers behind him with both hands out, caring, not touching. kɛ̀ɛ is old — old enough to refuse the arm. (_ low and flat, said without any fuss)
headline: kɛ̀ɛ.
scene: A very old man gripping a doorframe to haul himself up a high wooden step, jaw set, while his middle-aged daughter hovers behind with both hands raised and not quite touching him. A village house, bright doorway light.

mnemonic: Your lungs sit in your back, and your back is the part that comes after you. lǎng does both jobs: the back of the body, and after — whatever follows behind. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he twists to look behind him)
headline: lǎng.
scene: A man twisting round to look over his own shoulder at his bare back in a bathroom mirror, one hand reaching behind to a sore spot between his shoulder blades. Steam at the edge of the mirror, tiled wall, harsh ceiling light.

mnemonic: The florist turns each stem until not one of them juts out of line, then ties the whole thing off. tɕàt is arranging — putting things where they belong, nothing sticking out. (_ low and flat, each stem pressed down into place)
headline: tɕàt.
scene: A florist's hands turning and pressing the stems of a large bouquet into alignment on a workbench, a length of twine held ready between her teeth. Cut stems and leaves scattered across the bench, cool shopfront daylight.

mnemonic: Put a t on the front of her and you have thəə — which is what it means. A young woman steps up to the counter and the whole queue turns: her turn. (— flat and level, said without emphasis)
headline: thəə.
scene: A young woman stepping forward to a busy ticket counter as the people queueing behind her all turn to look at once. A bright station concourse, blurred crowd, high arched windows, morning light.

mnemonic: ที่ is the place and มา is coming: the thîi-maa of a thing is the place it came from. Follow the stream up past the village, past the trees, to the crack in the rock where it starts. (— the second syllable levels out, the walk over)
headline: thîi-maa.
scene: A hiker crouched at the head of a mountain stream where water seeps from a crack in mossy rock, cupping a handful of it, the stream winding far down the valley behind her. Cool green light, ferns, wet stone.

skip_reason: No English word matches the second syllable of thá-hǎan without shifting the vowel; harn, horn and harden all miss.

mnemonic: ต้อง is must — the giant tong in the flooded basement — and ต้องการ is what you must have. The man in the water is not asking for the tong. He needs it. (↓ falls hard on the first syllable, the water still rising)
headline: tɔ̂ng-gaan.
scene: A man standing chest-deep in the water of a flooding basement holding an enormous pair of iron tongs above his head with both arms, mouth open in a shout. Water pouring from a burst pipe, one swinging bulb.

mnemonic: Open the wardrobe and the moths have had the lot — every coat, every jumper, nothing left. tʰáng-mòt is all of it, the whole total, with mòt meaning used up entirely. (_ the second syllable drops flat, nothing left to say)
headline: tʰáng-mòt.
scene: An open wardrobe of ruined woollen clothes hanging in shreds with holes through every garment, a few moths still fluttering in the dim interior while a woman stands staring with her hands at her sides. A bedroom, grey window light.

skip_reason: No English anchor for rá-wàang; wrong and wang both shift the vowel and the compound is too long to carry a two-step pun.

mnemonic: A bowl of dice on the table and the old gambler tells him to take one — any die, it makes no difference which. dai is any: whichever one you like. (— flat and level, a shrug in the voice)
headline: …dai.
scene: A gaming table where a hand hovers over a wooden bowl heaped with identical white dice, while an old gambler opposite shrugs with both palms turned up. Green baize, stacked chips, a low hanging lamp, smoky air.

mnemonic: A long loaf cut into thick chunks, one chunk for each part of the day. Say chunk and drop the k — chûang — a stretch, a spell, a phase of time. (↓ falling, the knife coming down through the loaf)
headline: chûang.
scene: A wooden board with a long loaf cut into four thick uneven chunks and a knife resting across it, morning light from a window falling on the nearest chunk and leaving the far ones in shadow. Crumbs and flour dust.

mnemonic: The bill comes with everything on it — the drinks, the extra rice, the lot rolled into one number for the whole room. ruuam is gathering it all together: total, included. (— flat and level, one number, no argument)
headline: ruuam.
scene: A large round restaurant table of a dozen diners, one man at the centre holding up a single long curl of paper in both hands while everyone leans in towards it. Cleared plates, empty bottles, a warm overhead lamp.

mnemonic: A boy so keen to get it down that he starts before he sits, the pen already moving as he drops onto the bench. khǐan is to write, and the keenness is in the rising voice. (↑ rising, the voice climbs like his hand lifting off the page)
headline: khǐan.
scene: A schoolboy dropping onto a bench mid-stride with an open notebook on his knee and a pen already touching the page, his satchel still swinging from one shoulder. A courtyard, other children walking past, bright morning.

mnemonic: Every morning the same man takes the same seat at the same tea stall and puts his coin down without a word: the chai man. tɕhaai is a man — the male one, as against the woman at the next table. (— flat and level, the same note every morning)
headline: tɕhaai.
scene: A weathered man in a short-sleeved shirt sitting alone at the corner table of a small tea stall with a glass of milky tea and a single coin in front of him, staring out at the street. Early light, steam, empty chairs.

mnemonic: The door swings open for one second and the cat is through it and gone — oh, the cat. ʔoo-kàat is a chance: the gap, and whether you went through it. (_ the second syllable drops low, the door swinging shut)
headline: ʔoo-kàat!
scene: A cat streaking through the narrowing gap of a front door that is swinging shut, only its tail and hind legs still inside, while a man with shopping bags stands startled in the doorway. Hallway light, a rainy street behind.

mnemonic: The boss's eye is on the whole floor — one eye, and nobody moves. Put an n in front of eye and you have naai: mister, boss, the one you address properly. (— flat and level, with no warmth in it)
headline: naai.
scene: A supervisor standing on a raised platform at the end of a factory floor, hands behind his back, staring down the rows while every worker keeps their head bent over the bench. Long fluorescent strips, pale green machinery.

mnemonic: The whole class leans in over the one book on the desk, heads almost touching. riian is to learn — and Thais often soften that r towards an l, so leaning in gets you there. (— flat and level, a patient classroom note)
headline: riian.
scene: Six schoolchildren crowded round one small desk, all leaning in over a single open book with their heads nearly touching, one girl pointing at the page. A wooden classroom, ceiling fan, hot bright light through louvred windows.

mnemonic: A cicada in the tree sings so loudly the whole street looks up. Stretch sing into see-ang and you have sǐang: a sound, a voice, a noise. (↑ rising, the voice climbs the way the cicada's does)
headline: sǐang.
scene: A single large cicada clinging to the bark of a street tree with its wings blurred, while three pedestrians below have stopped and tilted their heads up towards it. Hot white daylight, dappled leaf shadow on the pavement.

mnemonic: Cut the bark and the sap tells you whether the tree is alive — the old forester knows by looking. Say sap with the long ah of father: sâap, the polite word for knowing. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the knife)
headline: sâap.
scene: An old forester pressing his thumb against a fresh cut on a tree trunk where pale sap is beading out, nodding slightly, a small knife in his other hand. Deep green forest shade, shafts of light through the leaves.

mnemonic: At the end of a long day a man hauls himself up the stairs like a ton of bricks — his own self, the heaviest thing he owns. ton is the self. (— flat and level, one step at a time)
headline: ton.
scene: An exhausted man hauling himself up a narrow concrete stairwell by the handrail, one foot on the next step, head down, jacket over his shoulder. A bare bulb, peeling paint, night outside a small window.

mnemonic: A pert little housemaid throws the shutters back and the whole room fills with light. Say pert without the r and with an unaspirated p — bpə̀ət — to open, to switch on. (_ low and flat, the shutters banging back)
headline: bpə̀ət.
scene: A young housemaid in an apron flinging a pair of tall wooden shutters wide open in a dark panelled room, morning light flooding across the floorboards with dust hanging in the beam. Her face turned into the light.

mnemonic: Cut the pie open and it is all in there: the filling, the steam, the whole dinner. phaai-nai is within — inside the crust, inside the hour, inside the building. (— flat and level, the steam rising evenly)
headline: phaai-nai.
scene: A steaming pie cut open on a kitchen table with one wedge lifted away on a slice to show the dark filling inside, steam rising into window light. An oven cloth, a chipped plate, a deep brown crust.

mnemonic: He came home from the beach with a tan instead of a burn, because somebody else took the chair in the full sun. tʰɛɛn is in place of — this one instead of that one. (— flat and level, said with a shrug)
headline: tʰɛɛn.
scene: Two men side by side on a beach: one golden brown and relaxed in the shade of a palm, the other lobster red and wincing in the open sun. Deck chairs, turquoise sea, hard afternoon light.

skip_reason: No English word carries phûak; pack, puck and poke each shift the vowel.

mnemonic: One photograph of the whole group, and it is the only picture of them all together. Take the roup off group — rûup — a picture, an image, a photo. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the shutter closes)
headline: rûup.
scene: An old framed group photograph of a large family standing in rows outside a village house, hanging slightly crooked on a bare wall from a single nail, a vase of flowers on a shelf below. Warm side light, faded paper.

mnemonic: She lowers the Wang handbag onto the table with both hands, squares it up and takes her hands away. She is not putting it down, she is placing it. waang is exactly that: setting a thing down deliberately and leaving it. (— flat and level, the bag settling without a sound)
headline: waang.
scene: A woman's two hands lowering an expensive black leather handbag onto a polished café table and squaring it precisely, her face out of frame. A marble surface, a coffee cup pushed aside, bright window reflections.

mnemonic: The naan comes out of the oven longer than the table and it takes the whole evening to get through it. naan is a long time — the bread and the waiting are the same word. (— flat and level, the evening going on and on)
headline: naan.
scene: An enormous naan bread stretching the full length of a restaurant table and hanging off both ends, four diners along one side tearing pieces from it while a waiter carries in more. Warm light, a tandoor glowing behind.

mnemonic: phûu is the one-who and yǐng is the yin: the person of the yin side. Her name is called and a woman rises out of the seated crowd. (↑ the second syllable climbs, the head lifting with it)
headline: phûu-yǐng.
scene: A woman standing up out of a seated crowd at a village ceremony, chin lifting, hands pressed together in front of her, everyone else still seated and turned towards her. Folding chairs, marigold garlands, bright outdoor shade.

mnemonic: The whole village sang together at the festival, and afterwards every one of them came to the same long table to eat. sǎng-khom is society: the people who sang and then came — the ones who do both those things together. (— the second syllable levels out, everyone seated at last)
headline: sǎng-khom.
scene: A long communal table under strings of bulbs in a village square, forty people of all ages seated shoulder to shoulder passing dishes along, a few still standing and clapping. Warm night, food steam, dark trees beyond.

mnemonic: Rows and rows of jam jars on the pantry shelf, and the only question anybody asks is how many: the jam-number. tɕam-nuuan is an amount, a quantity, a count. (— flat and level, counting along the row)
headline: tɕam-nuuan.
scene: A long pantry shelf packed end to end with identical jars of dark red jam, a woman halfway along it with one hand raised, mid-count. Cool larder light from a small high window, a stone floor.
